title: How to stop mass shootings, with Jillian Peterson, PhD

sentences.en: It is painful to grasp, but mass shootings have become a common occurrence in the United States.
sentences.zh: 虽然难以接受，但大规模枪击事件在美国已成家常便饭。

sentences.en: Whether at a school, a church or synagogue, or a supermarket, these incidents may shock, but they no longer surprise.
sentences.zh: 无论是学校、教堂还是犹太会堂，亦或是超市，这些事件可能会让人震惊，但已不再让人意外。

sentences.en: Cities, small towns, and schools across the country are now associated forever with this form of violence.
sentences.zh: 全国各地的城市、小镇和学校，现在都永远与这种形式的暴力联系在了一起。

sentences.en: Names like Columbine, Sandy Hook, Parkland, and Uvalde, Aurora, Charleston, Boulder, and Buffalo.
sentences.zh: 诸如科伦拜恩、桑迪胡克、帕克兰和乌瓦尔德，还有奥罗拉、查尔斯顿、博尔德和布法罗这些名字。

sentences.en: Each time, politicians spar over whether to blame guns, mental illness, or moral decay for the massacres.
sentences.zh: 每一次，政客们都会争论不休，究竟该将这些大屠杀归咎于枪支、精神疾病还是道德沦丧。

sentences.en: Against this backdrop, it's easy to feel hopeless and to think that mass shootings have simply become an unavoidable part of American life.
sentences.zh: 在此背景下，人们很容易感到绝望，认为大规模枪击事件已经成为美国生活不可避免的一部分。

sentences.en: But, according to some researchers, there is hope.
sentences.zh: 但据一些研究人员称，希望依然存在。

sentences.en: By studying what drives mass shooters, they say, we can better understand the causes of America's mass shooting epidemic and perhaps learn how to stop it.
sentences.zh: 他们表示，通过研究是什么驱使了大规模枪击案枪手，我们可以更好地了解美国大规模枪击流行病的成因，并或许能找到阻止它的方法。

sentences.en: What drives most mass shooters?
sentences.zh: 是什么驱使了大多数大规模枪击案枪手？

sentences.en: What do they have in common?
sentences.zh: 他们有什么共同点？

sentences.en: What role, if any, does mental illness play in their actions?
sentences.zh: 精神疾病在他们的行为中扮演了什么角色（如果有的话）？

sentences.en: What about racist and extremist ideologies?
sentences.zh: 种族主义和极端主义意识形态呢？

sentences.en: What about the internet?
sentences.zh: 互联网呢？

sentences.en: Does media coverage of mass shootings drive copycat crimes?
sentences.zh: 关于大规模枪击事件的媒体报道是否会引发模仿犯罪？

sentences.en: Do active shooter drills and armed guards at schools save lives?
sentences.zh: 学校里的现役枪手演习和武装警卫能否拯救生命？

sentences.en: And what can be done in workplaces, houses of worship, and other venues to make the next mass shooting less likely?
sentences.zh: 为了降低下一次大规模枪击事件发生的可能性，工作场所、礼拜场所和其他场所可以采取什么措施？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学说话》，这是美国心理学协会的旗舰播客，探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: My guest today is Dr. Jillian Peterson, a psychologist and associate professor of criminology and criminal justice at Hamline University in St. Paul, Minnesota.
sentences.zh: 我今天的嘉宾是吉莉安·彼得森博士，她是一名心理学家，也是明尼苏达州圣保罗哈姆林大学的犯罪学和刑事司法副教授。

sentences.en: She is a co-founder of the Violence Project, a nonprofit organization that has compiled the database of every mass shooting in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 她是“暴力项目”的联合创始人，该非营利组织汇编了自1966年以来美国所有大规模枪击事件的数据库。

sentences.en: since 1966.
sentences.zh: 自1966年以来。

sentences.en: She and her colleagues have also interviewed friends, family, victims, and in some cases, the perpetrators themselves, to compile detailed life histories of some 180 mass shooters.
sentences.zh: 她和同事还采访了朋友、家人、受害者，以及在某些情况下的行凶者本人，以编纂大约180名大规模枪击案凶手的详细生平。

sentences.en: The goal of the Violence Project is to use this information to better understand mass shooters' pathways to violence and develop strategies to stop them.
sentences.zh: “暴力项目”的目标是利用这些信息更好地了解大规模枪击案凶手走向暴力的路径，并制定阻止他们的策略。

sentences.en: Dr. Peterson's book, The Violence Project, How to Stop a Mass Shooting Epidemic, co-authored with her colleague, Dr. James Densley, was published in 2021.
sentences.zh: 彼得森博士与其同事詹姆斯·邓斯利博士合著的书籍《暴力项目：如何制止大规模枪击流行病》于2021年出版。

sentences.en: Thank you for joining me today, Dr. Peterson.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢您今天能来，彼得森博士。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for having me.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: I'm happy to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里。

sentences.en: So, I just mentioned that the Violence Project has compiled a database of every mass shooting in the United States since 1966.
sentences.zh: 那么，我刚才提到“暴力项目”汇编了自1966年以来美国所有大规模枪击事件的数据库。

sentences.en: So, first, how did you define mass shooting?
sentences.zh: 首先，你们是如何定义大规模枪击事件的？

sentences.en: Because not everyone who counts these incidents defines mass shooting in the same way.
sentences.zh: 因为并非所有统计这些事件的人对大规模枪击的定义都一样。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's an important question because depending on how you define a mass shooting, you can say there's been five or six in the past year or hundreds.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个重要的问题，因为根据你对大规模枪击的定义，你可以说过去一年发生了五六起，也可以说有几百起。

sentences.en: So, we use a pretty narrow definition, which is four or more people killed in a public space, not including the perpetrator,
sentences.zh: 所以，我们使用的是一个相当狭窄的定义，即在公共场所造成四人或四人以上死亡，不包括行凶者在内，

sentences.en: and the shooting is not related to other underlying criminal activity, and it's not a domestic violence situation.
sentences.zh: 并且枪击事件与其它潜在的犯罪活动无关，也不是家庭暴力情况。

sentences.en: So, many of us have the impression that mass shootings are on the increase in the United States.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们许多人都有这样一种印象，即美国的大规模枪击事件正在增加。

sentences.en: Is that borne out by the data you've been collecting?
sentences.zh: 你们收集的数据证实了这一点吗？

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: So, we're tracking these incidents where four or more people have been killed, and we see that the worst incidents on record were 2017, 2018, 2019.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们一直在追踪那些造成四人或四人以上死亡的事件，我们发现有记录以来最糟糕的年份是2017年、2018年、2019年。

sentences.en: Those were the worst years.
sentences.zh: 那些是最糟糕的年份。

sentences.en: Then we had this pause during the pandemic because public spaces weren't open.
sentences.zh: 然后我们在疫情期间经历了一段暂停，因为公共场所没有开放。

sentences.en: And when we did reopen in 2020, 2021, we've seen this kind of resurgence, especially this summer.
sentences.zh: 当我们在2020年、2021年重新开放时，我们看到了这种死灰复燃，特别是今年夏天。

sentences.en: We had one of the worst sort of month or two on record in terms of mass shootings.
sentences.zh: 就大规模枪击事件而言，我们经历了有记录以来最糟糕的一两个月之一。

sentences.en: What do you attribute this increase to?
sentences.zh: 你将这种增长归因于什么？

sentences.en: It's hard to say exactly.
sentences.zh: 很难说得准。

sentences.en: I think it's a number of factors at play.
sentences.zh: 我认为有许多因素在起作用。

sentences.en: One is that during the pandemic, a number of risk factors for mass shootings we know increased.
sentences.zh: 其一是，在疫情期间，我们所知的大规模枪击事件的许多风险因素都有所增加。

sentences.en: So, things like isolation, hopelessness, spending increasing amounts of time online, suicidality.
sentences.zh: 比如孤立、绝望、花越来越多的时间在网上、有自杀倾向。

sentences.en: We also had record gun sales in this country.
sentences.zh: 我们这个国家的枪支销量也创下了历史新高。

sentences.en: So, there's just more access to firearMs.
sentences.zh: 所以，只是更容易获得枪支了。

sentences.en: And what have you learned about the profile of the people who commit mass shootings?
sentences.zh: 关于犯下大规模枪击事件的人的个人资料，你们了解到了什么？

sentences.en: What do these men, and they are mostly men, have in common?
sentences.zh: 这些男性（他们绝大多数是男性）有什么共同点？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, in our database, it's 98% men.
sentences.zh: 因此，在我们的数据库中，98%是男性。

sentences.en: There's four women in the database.
sentences.zh: 数据库中有四名女性。

sentences.en: Two of them perpetrated the shooting with a man.
sentences.zh: 其中两人与一名男性共同实施了枪击。

sentences.en: So, we see this common pathway.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们看到了这条共同的路径。

sentences.en: And, of course, it's a little different for each person.
sentences.zh: 当然，对每个人来说都略有不同。

sentences.en: But this pathway seems to start with really significant early childhood trauma.
sentences.zh: 但这条路径似乎始于非常严重的早期童年创伤。

sentences.en: So, things like physical abuse, sexual abuse, suicide of a parent, domestic violence in the home.
sentences.zh: 比如身体虐待、性虐待、父母自杀、家里的家庭暴力。

sentences.en: Over time, that individual becomes angry, becomes isolated, becomes hopeless.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，这个人变得愤怒、孤立、绝望。

sentences.en: There's a lot of self-loathing there.
sentences.zh: 那里有很多自我厌恶。

sentences.en: Many of them are suicidal and attempt suicide before doing a mass shooting.
sentences.zh: 他们中的许多人都有自杀倾向，并在实施大规模枪击之前尝试过自杀。

sentences.en: Then, that self-loathing kind of turns outward, and it becomes, whose fault is this?
sentences.zh: 然后，这种自我厌恶转向外部，变成了，这是谁的错？

sentences.en: Who do I blame for the fact that I feel this way?
sentences.zh: 我该怪谁让我有这种感觉？

sentences.en: So, school shooters blame their school.
sentences.zh: 所以，学校枪手责怪他们的学校。

sentences.en: Workplace shooters blame their workplace.
sentences.zh: 工作场所枪手责怪他们的工作场所。

sentences.en: Other people blame, you know, religious groups or racial groups or women.
sentences.zh: 其他人责怪，你知道的，宗教团体、种族群体或女性。

sentences.en: Perpetrators tend to be radicalized through studying other shooters before them.
sentences.zh: 行凶者往往通过研究他们之前的其他枪手而被激进化。

sentences.en: Many of them spend time on the Internet in kind of these dark chat rooms where violence is really celebrated and validated.
sentences.zh: 他们中的许多人在互联网上的一些黑暗聊天室里度过时间，在那里暴力确实受到颂扬和认可。

sentences.en: And then, they go into this act knowing it's their final act.
sentences.zh: 然后，他们在明知这是最后一次行动的情况下开始行动。

sentences.en: So, they're kind of actively suicidal, planning to die in the act.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们有点处于积极的自杀状态，计划在行动中死去。

sentences.en: They have access to the firearms that they need.
sentences.zh: 他们能够获得所需的枪支。

sentences.en: And many of them leak their plans.
sentences.zh: 他们中的许多人泄露了他们的计划。

sentences.en: Many of them tell other people they're thinking about violence before they do it.
sentences.zh: 他们中的许多人在实施暴力之前告诉其他人他们正在考虑暴力。

sentences.en: And then,
sentences.zh: 然后，

sentences.en: they go out and they choose a location that's symbolic of their grievance with the world because they're looking for this fame and notoriety in their death that they didn't have in their life.
sentences.zh: 他们走出去，选择一个象征着他们对世界不满的地点，因为他们正在寻找生前没有的名气和恶名，以便在死后获得。

sentences.en: What role, if any, does mental illness play in mass shootings?
sentences.zh: 精神疾病在大规模枪击事件中起到了什么作用（如果有的话）？

sentences.en: We always hear from local leaders, politicians, law enforcement, that whoever perpetrated a mass shooting must be mentally ill.
sentences.zh: 我们总是从地方领袖、政客、执法部门那里听到，无论谁犯下了大规模枪击事件，肯定都有精神疾病。

sentences.en: Is that always the case?
sentences.zh: 事实总是如此吗？

sentences.en: It's not.
sentences.zh: 并非如此。

sentences.en: And this is one of the initial questions that kind of got me into this research because before mass shootings, I studied the link between mental illness and crime and violence.
sentences.zh: 这也是最初让我进入这项研究的问题之一，因为在大规模枪击事件之前，我研究了精神疾病与犯罪和暴力之间的联系。

sentences.en: And it was something that we always turn to instinctually.
sentences.zh: 这是我们本能上总是会转向的东西。

sentences.en: It's like we don't understand this.
sentences.zh: 就像我们不理解这一点一样。

sentences.en: So, somebody must be mentally ill.
sentences.zh: 所以，某人肯定有精神疾病。

sentences.en: So, we looked really deeply at histories of mental illness and diagnoses, at previous counseling, psychiatric medication, anything that we could find.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们深入研究了精神疾病和诊断的历史、以前的咨询、精神科药物，以及我们能找到的任何东西。

sentences.en: So, we did find most mass shooters, about two-thirds, have some sort of mental health history.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们确实发现大多数大规模枪击案凶手，大约三分之二，都有某种心理健康史。

sentences.en: That being said, there was no one diagnosis that was consistent over time.
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，没有哪一种诊断结果是随着时间推移保持一致的。

sentences.en: Thought disorders were overrepresented compared to the general population.
sentences.zh: 与普通人口相比，思维障碍的比例过高。

sentences.en: But when we tried to look at what role does psychosis play in leading to a mass shooting, it was about 10% of perpetrators.
sentences.zh: 但当我们试图研究精神病在导致大规模枪击事件中起什么作用时，大约占行凶者的10%。

sentences.en: We could say psychosis really was an active role here, whereas the other 90%, it's much more complicated.
sentences.zh: 我们可以说精神病在这里确实起到了积极的作用，而其余90%则要复杂得多。

sentences.en: So, even perpetrators who did have a history of mental illness, it's like it's this complex build, this complex pathway to violence.
sentences.zh: 所以，即使是有精神病史的行凶者，这也就像是一种复杂的积聚，一条通往暴力的复杂路径。

sentences.en: And mental illness is not typically the thing that is pushing them over the edge.
sentences.zh: 而精神疾病通常不是将他们推向边缘的东西。

sentences.en: We see that perpetrators are in crisis before the shooting.
sentences.zh: 我们看到行凶者在枪击发生前处于危机之中。

sentences.en: That might be related to mental illness.
sentences.zh: 这可能与精神疾病有关。

sentences.en: It might be not.
sentences.zh: 也可能无关。

sentences.en: We see that they're suicidal.
sentences.zh: 我们看到他们有自杀倾向。

sentences.en: But trying to sort of pick out a diagnosis and say, this is what these perpetrators have in common, you absolutely can't do that.
sentences.zh: 但是试图挑出一种诊断并说，这就是这些行凶者的共同点，你绝对做不到这一点。

sentences.en: Do we know enough at this point to predict who might become a mass shooter?
sentences.zh: 目前我们对谁可能成为大规模枪击案凶手有足够的了解来进行预测吗？

sentences.en: I know APA did a study a number of years ago.
sentences.zh: 我知道APA在多年前做过一项研究。

sentences.en: There's very limited information back then.
sentences.zh: 那时的信息非常有限。

sentences.en: There's maybe a little bit more today.
sentences.zh: 今天可能稍微多了一点。

sentences.en: But we were not able to come up with any kind of a guideline for this person has these five factors and therefore, given the opportunity, is going to go kill a bunch of people.
sentences.zh: 但我们没能提出任何形式的指导方针，说这个人有这五个因素，因此，只要有机会，他就会去杀害一群人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: No, we're not able to do that because for each person who has those five factors, you know, 99.99% of them would never do this.
sentences.zh: 不，我们做不到这一点，因为对于每一个拥有这五个因素的人来说，你知道的，他们当中99.99%的人永远不会这样做。

sentences.en: And so, it really is like finding a needle in a haystack.
sentences.zh: 所以，这真的就像大海捞针一样。

sentences.en: What we do know is that perpetrators who do this tend to tell other people that they're thinking about it, tend to talk about violence, school shooters.
sentences.zh: 我们所知道的是，做这件事的行凶者往往会告诉其他人他们正在考虑这件事，往往会谈论暴力，学校枪手。

sentences.en: It's about 80% of them tell their classmates that they're planning on it.
sentences.zh: 大约80%的人会告诉他们的同学他们正在计划这件事。

sentences.en: So, we know there's these warning signs.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们知道有这些警告信号。

sentences.en: We know they're actively suicidal, in crisis, behavior is changing.
sentences.zh: 我们知道他们正处于积极的自杀状态、危机中，行为正在改变。

sentences.en: And so, what we advocate for is building systems in schools and organizations that can watch for this type of behavior, for this leakage, for kids in crisis,
sentences.zh: 因此，我们所倡导的是在学校和组织中建立能够关注这种类型行为、这种泄露、关注危机中的孩子的系统，

sentences.en: provide them with resources, not because we think, oh, here's the next school shooter, but it's here's somebody in crisis who needs some intervention.
sentences.zh: 为他们提供资源，不是因为我们认为，哦，下一个学校枪手就在这里，而是这里有一个需要一些干预的处于危机中的人。

sentences.en: And that might prevent a school shooting.
sentences.zh: 那可能会阻止一场校园枪击案。

sentences.en: It might prevent a whole lot of things, though.
sentences.zh: 不过，这也可能会阻止很多其他事情。

sentences.en: There's kind of this diffusion of benefit to these systems where you're preventing suicides, you're preventing violence, but there's no way I can give you, here's the 20 things,
sentences.zh: 这些系统有一种效益扩散，你可以防止自杀，可以防止暴力，但我无法给你列出20件事，

sentences.en: and if you check these boxes, here's your school shooter.
sentences.zh: 如果你勾选了这些方框，这里就是你的校园枪手。

sentences.en: So, you mentioned leakage in schools in particular where shooters may be letting people know that they're planning something.
sentences.zh: 所以，你特别提到了学校里的泄露现象，枪手可能会让人们知道他们在策划什么。

sentences.en: And in schools, you know, we're very focused on either these active shooter drills or whether they want to bring in armed guards or other people who might somehow prevent this.
sentences.zh: 而在学校里，你知道的，我们非常关注这些现役枪手演习，或者他们是否想引进武装警卫或其他可能以某种方式阻止这种情况的人。

sentences.en: But wouldn't it make more sense to be training the children how to recognize these factors and then what to do in the event that they see something and then they should say something,
sentences.zh: 但是，与其这样，不是更有意义去培训孩子们如何识别这些因素，然后在他们看到某些东西时该怎么做，然后他们应该说出来吗，

sentences.en: to whom do they say it?
sentences.zh: 他们应该对谁说？

sentences.en: Are we doing that?
sentences.zh: 我们在这样做吗？

sentences.en: Not really yet.
sentences.zh: 还没有真正这样做。

sentences.en: I don't think we are quite there yet.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们还没有完全做到这一点。

sentences.en: I think for a long time, really, so post-Columbine, it's been about reducing casualties, right?
sentences.zh: 我认为很长一段时间以来，实际上，自科伦拜恩事件以来，重点一直是减少伤亡，对吧？

sentences.en: How do we send our kids in bulletproof backpacks and make these fancy security systems and these strong doors and active shooter training?
sentences.zh: 我们如何让我们的孩子背上防弹背包，制造这些高档的安全系统、坚固的门和现役枪手训练？

sentences.en: That was all based on this premise that the person doing the shooting was not a child in the building, right?
sentences.zh: 这一切都是基于这样一个前提：开枪的人不是大楼里的孩子，对吧？

sentences.en: We now know that 90% of the time, it's a current or former student.
sentences.zh: 我们现在知道，90%的情况下，是现任或前任学生。

sentences.en: This is a kid sitting next to our kid in class, walking in and out of the security and running through all the drills, right?
sentences.zh: 这是一个坐在我们孩子旁边上课的孩子，在安检中进进出出，经历所有演习的孩子，对吧？

sentences.en: This is a child who's an insider, not an outsider.
sentences.zh: 这是一个内部的孩子，而不是外部的人。

sentences.en: And that really shifts your perspective about how we prevent this.
sentences.zh: 这确实改变了你对我们如何防止这种情况发生的看法。

sentences.en: In some ways, it's harder because it's not a kid you can keep out with security.
sentences.zh: 在某些方面这更难，因为这不是一个你可以用安保挡在门外的孩子。

sentences.en: It's a kid coming to school every day.
sentences.zh: 这是一个每天来学校上学的孩子。

sentences.en: But in some ways, it's easier because we can look out for these warning signs.
sentences.zh: 但在某些方面这更容易，因为我们可以留意这些警告信号。

sentences.en: We can do things like build really strong, trusting relationships between kids and adults in the building so kids feel safe disclosing things.
sentences.zh: 我们可以做一些事情，比如在大楼里的孩子和成年人之间建立非常牢固、充满信任的关系，这样孩子们在透露事情时会感到安全。

sentences.en: And a lot of times, kids don't disclose things because we have this really punitive response.
sentences.zh: 很多时候，孩子们不愿透露事情，是因为我们有这种非常惩罚性的反应。

sentences.en: You know, they're not going to tell on their friend and get their friend kicked out of school or their friend criminally charged and sent to prison.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们不会告发他们的朋友，让他们的朋友被赶出学校，或者让他们的朋友受到刑事指控并送进监狱。

sentences.en: But they might report their friend if their response is kind of compassionate, it's about care, it's about connecting to resources.
sentences.zh: 但如果反应是富有同情心的、关于关怀的、关于连接资源的，他们可能会举报他们的朋友。

sentences.en: So quite a few of the recent shootings have targeted Black Americans or Asian Americans, Jews, other minority groups.
sentences.zh: 所以最近的一些枪击事件针对的是美籍非裔或亚裔美国人、犹太人和其他少数群体。

sentences.en: What percentage of mass shootings involve racist or extremist ideology?
sentences.zh: 有多少比例的大规模枪击事件涉及种族主义或极端主义意识形态？

sentences.en: You know, that's not a number off the top of my head.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这不是一个我能随口说出的数字。

sentences.en: It's actually a minority of them.
sentences.zh: 实际上这只占少数。

sentences.en: Um, we have seen an increase in hate driven mass shootings where there is a specific hateful ideology associated with it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们已经看到仇恨驱使的大规模枪击事件有所增加，其中存在与之相关的特定仇恨意识形态。

sentences.en: What we're interested in is kind of how do people get to that hateful ideology?
sentences.zh: 我们感兴趣的是人们是如何陷入那种仇恨意识形态的？

sentences.en: And one thing that we found is that hate actually comes relatively late upon the pathway to violence.
sentences.zh: 我们发现的一点是，仇恨在通往暴力的道路上其实出现得相对较晚。

sentences.en: It's like they are in crisis, they're suicidal, they're self-loathing, they're angry at the world.
sentences.zh: 就像他们身处危机之中，有自杀倾向，自我厌恶，对世界感到愤怒。

sentences.en: And then they find this thing to blame that they now hate.
sentences.zh: 然后他们找到了这个他们现在痛恨的、可以怪罪的东西。

sentences.en: And sometimes they find it because they stumble onto a website.
sentences.zh: 有时他们找到它是偶然撞上了一个网站。

sentences.en: But these are not, you know, young people being raised in households full of racist ideology.
sentences.zh: 但这些并不是，你知道的，在充满种族主义意识形态的家庭中养大的年轻人。

sentences.en: This is sometimes they stumble onto it a month or two months before the shooting.
sentences.zh: 有时这是他们在枪击发生前一个月或两个月偶然碰上的。

sentences.en: And they couldn't even really tell you a lot of details about it.
sentences.zh: 而且他们甚至无法真正告诉你关于它的很多细节。

sentences.en: But it's they glom onto this thing.
sentences.zh: 但他们就是死死缠住了这个东西。

sentences.en: And I think it's really important that we tackle that hate, especially, I think,
sentences.zh: 我认为我们必须应对这种仇恨，特别是，我认为，

sentences.en: when we can talk about social media and where young people are getting access to this type of hate online.
sentences.zh: 我们可以讨论社交媒体以及年轻人如何在网上接触到这类仇恨言论。

sentences.en: But it's also important to look at what's underlying that so we can prevent people from getting to that point.
sentences.zh: 但同样重要的是，我们要探究其背后的深层原因，从而防止人们走到那一步。

sentences.en: And so it's sort of both of those pieces.
sentences.zh: 所以这可以说是这两个方面共同作用的结果。

sentences.en: So we talked a minute ago about how most of the mass shooters you've identified are male.
sentences.zh: 我们刚才提到，你所识别的大多数枪击案凶手都是男性。

sentences.en: Most of them are also white males.
sentences.zh: 他们绝大多数也是白人男性。

sentences.en: And I'm just wondering how much a sense of disenfranchisement is playing a role here, whether it's, you know, feminism has ruined my life or that black guy took my job.
sentences.zh: 我在想，这种被剥夺权利的感觉在这里面起到了多大作用？无论是“女权主义毁了我的生活”还是“那个黑人抢了我的工作”。

sentences.en: Or, you know, just these feelings of the world is now unfair to white men.
sentences.zh: 或者仅仅是“这个世界现在对白人很不公平”这种感觉。

sentences.en: Is that a factor that you see?
sentences.zh: 这是你所看到的一个因素吗？

sentences.en: It is a factor.
sentences.zh: 这确实是一个因素。

sentences.en: I think it's a really hard factor to measure.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个很难量化的因素。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But we can we talk about it in the book.
sentences.zh: 但我们在书中讨论过这一点。

sentences.en: We have a chapter called America and we can talk about guns in America and we can talk about violence in America.
sentences.zh: 我们有一章叫做“美国”，我们可以讨论美国的枪支问题，也可以讨论美国的暴力问题。

sentences.en: But there's also this other piece here that I think is about disenfranchised white men.
sentences.zh: 但这里还有另一个因素，我认为与那些感到被剥夺权利的白人男性有关。

sentences.en: And there's this piece that we see in these perpetrators where it's like I was owed this thing.
sentences.zh: 我们在这些凶手身上看到了这样一种心理，就好像是“我本来就该拥有这一切”。

sentences.en: I expected to be in this place in my life where I'm not.
sentences.zh: 我本该在生活里达到某种我目前还没到达的高度。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The world owes me success or owes me a girlfriend or owes me a job or owes me whatever.
sentences.zh: 世界欠我成功，或者欠我一个女朋友，或者欠我一份工作，或者欠我别的什么。

sentences.en: That I think when you don't get that, then somehow you're angrier and it must be someone's fault.
sentences.zh: 当他们得不到这些时，就会变得更加愤怒，并觉得这一定是别人的错。

sentences.en: I do think that level of kind of entitlement is a big piece of this that goes along with being a white man.
sentences.zh: 我确实认为，这种程度的特权心态是导致这一现象的重要原因，它往往伴随着白人男性的身份出现。

sentences.en: You know, a lot of other people don't expect that and they don't feel that they're owed.
sentences.zh: 你知道，很多其他人并没有这种期待，也不会觉得自己理应得到什么。

sentences.en: And so I do think we do see that.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为我们的确看到了这种现象。

sentences.en: But again, it's hard to really measure and grasp.
sentences.zh: 但话又说回来，这确实很难真正去衡量和把握。

sentences.en: Are there similar patterns among the rare people of color you have found who do commit mass shootings?
sentences.zh: 在那些极少数实施大规模枪击的有色人种中，有没有发现类似的模式？

sentences.en: Yeah, you do see.
sentences.zh: 是的，你确实能看到。

sentences.en: So perpetrators are majority white, but it's only around 60 percent white.
sentences.zh: 凶手大部分是白人，但白人比例其实只占60%左右。

sentences.en: So you do see perpetrators of color.
sentences.zh: 所以你也会看到有色人种凶手。

sentences.en: You see a lot more workplace shootings perpetrated by men of color.
sentences.zh: 你会发现有色人种男性实施的职场枪击案要多得多。

sentences.en: A lot of times it's somebody.
sentences.zh: 很多时候凶手就是某个人。

sentences.en: So they tend to be kind of factories, warehouses.
sentences.zh: 这些案子往往发生在工厂、仓库这类地方。

sentences.en: They tend to be in the south, kind of the primary employer of the town.
sentences.zh: 它们通常发生在南方，往往是当地的主要雇主所在地。

sentences.en: And it's typically somebody who just got fired.
sentences.zh: 而且通常是刚被解雇的人。

sentences.en: And so they lose their identity.
sentences.zh: 于是他们失去了身份认同。

sentences.en: They lose their resources.
sentences.zh: 他们失去了经济来源。

sentences.en: They lose social services, all the things that we tie to employment.
sentences.zh: 他们失去了社会福利，失去了所有我们与工作挂钩的东西。

sentences.en: Somebody who just got fired is pushed over the edge.
sentences.zh: 一个刚被解雇的人被逼到了绝境。

sentences.en: And oftentimes it's not that well planned.
sentences.zh: 而且很多时候，这并没有经过周密的策划。

sentences.en: It's like they go to their car and pull their handgun that they legally own out of their glove box and go back in and commit a mass shooting.
sentences.zh: 就像是他们走到车前，从杂物箱里拿出合法拥有的手枪，然后折返回去实施大规模枪击。

sentences.en: Those have actually gone down in recent years.
sentences.zh: 这类案件近年来实际上有所减少。

sentences.en: We see a lot more of those in kind of 80, 90s, early 2000s.
sentences.zh: 我们在80年代、90年代和2000年代初期看到了更多这类案件。

sentences.en: You've written about social contagion, people who are at risk of committing violent acts.
sentences.zh: 你写过关于社会传染的内容，也就是那些有暴力倾向的人。

sentences.en: They see news stories about a shooting and are spurred to go out and do the same thing.
sentences.zh: 他们看到关于枪击案的新闻报道，就会受到刺激去效仿并做出同样的事情。

sentences.en: Are there ways that the media could cover these events differently to lessen the likelihood of copycat shootings?
sentences.zh: 媒体有没有什么不同的报道方式，可以减少这种模仿性枪击事件发生的可能性？

sentences.en: There is.
sentences.zh: 有的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: There's this wonderful organization called No Notoriety, which was founded by Tom and Karen Teaves, who lost their son.
sentences.zh: 有一个非常棒的组织叫“拒绝声誉”（No Notoriety），由汤姆和凯伦·蒂夫斯创立，他们的儿子不幸遇难。

sentences.en: He was killed in the Aurora, Colorado shooting.
sentences.zh: 他在科罗拉多州奥罗拉枪击案中遇害。

sentences.en: And they were really appalled with the level of coverage that that perpetrator received in the media.
sentences.zh: 他们对媒体给予那个凶手的报道热度感到非常震惊。

sentences.en: His face was everywhere, all over cable news, on the front of newspapers and magazines, where their son just kind of faded away and didn't get that same type of attention.
sentences.zh: 他的脸无处不在，铺天盖地都是有线新闻，各大报纸和杂志的头版也都是他，而他们的儿子却渐渐被人遗忘，没有得到同样的关注。

sentences.en: And we do know that perpetrators are looking for that attention.
sentences.zh: 我们确实知道，凶手正是在寻求这种关注。

sentences.en: We call these a type of performance crimes because they are meant to be watched and witnessed.
sentences.zh: 我们称之为表演型犯罪，因为它们就是为了被观看、被目睹而产生的。

sentences.en: They're meant to create fear.
sentences.zh: 它们是为了制造恐惧。

sentences.en: They're meant to have their manifesto go viral.
sentences.zh: 它们是为了让自己的宣言在网上疯传。

sentences.en: They're meant to have their name make the history books alongside all these other names.
sentences.zh: 它们是为了让自己的名字和所有其他这些名字一起载入史册。

sentences.en: And so there's this piece of this that when we watch and when we consume it,
sentences.zh: 所以这就意味着，当我们观看并消费这些内容时，

sentences.en: we're kind of giving them the attention that they're looking for and then also inspiring the next person looking for that same level of attention.
sentences.zh: 我们其实是在给予他们想要的关注，同时也激励了下一个正在寻求同样关注度的人。

sentences.en: So the No Notoriety Protocol is focused, it's similar to actually the way that media covers suicides, because we know celebrity suicides, there's a contagion aspect to that.
sentences.zh: 因此，“拒绝声誉”协议的侧重点，实际上类似于媒体报道自杀事件的方式，因为我们知道名人自杀具有传染性。

sentences.en: And so now journalists are trained in how to cover suicides in a way to not give details about how the suicide was committed,
sentences.zh: 所以现在记者们接受了如何报道自杀的培训，不透露自杀的具体细节，

sentences.en: to kind of minimize coverage so as not to amplify that contagion.
sentences.zh: 尽量减少报道，以免放大这种传染效应。

sentences.en: It's similar for mass shootings.
sentences.zh: 大规模枪击事件也是如此。

sentences.en: We can talk about the mass shooting.
sentences.zh: 我们可以讨论枪击案本身。

sentences.en: We can talk about the victims, the first responders, but not to give the perpetrator that level of attention that they're looking for.
sentences.zh: 我们可以讨论受害者、急救人员，但绝不能给予凶手他们所寻求的那种关注。

sentences.en: For a significant number of mass shooters, the act is a way to end their lives.
sentences.zh: 对于相当一部分大规模枪击案凶手来说，这种行为是他们结束生命的一种方式。

sentences.en: I mean, you've said that they're either going to be killed by law enforcement officers or they may end up shooting themselves.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你曾说过他们要么被执法人员击毙，要么最终自杀。

sentences.en: Is there a way to use some of the suicide prevention strategies that psychology has developed to reduce the number of mass shootings?
sentences.zh: 有没有办法利用心理学发展出的自杀干预策略来减少大规模枪击事件的数量？

sentences.en: I really think that there is.
sentences.zh: 我真的觉得可以。

sentences.en: This was a real kind of eye-opening moment for me.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说是一个真正大开眼界的时刻。

sentences.en: We interviewed a number of perpetrators.
sentences.zh: 我们采访了许多凶手。

sentences.en: This was consistently, they said that they went in to be killed by police or they went in planning to kill themselves.
sentences.zh: 他们一直都在说，他们进去就是为了被警察击毙，或者他们进去时就打算自杀。

sentences.en: The number of perpetrators who attempted suicide beforehand was astounding.
sentences.zh: 事发前企图自杀的凶手数量令人震惊。

sentences.en: And we realized nobody goes in planning to come out.
sentences.zh: 我们意识到，没有人是带着活着出来的打算进去的。

sentences.en: There's no like put on a disguise and race for the border.
sentences.zh: 没有什么化装易容然后一路狂奔到边境的情节。

sentences.en: It's you go in, you have to be caught for this in order to get the attention that you want.
sentences.zh: 你走进去，必须在这里被捕才能获得你想要的关注。

sentences.en: So you have to either be killed, kill yourself, or spend the rest of your life in prison.
sentences.zh: 所以你只能选择被击毙、自杀，或者在监狱里度过余生。

sentences.en: It's a final act.
sentences.zh: 这是他们的最后行动。

sentences.en: And for me, who I have a background in suicide prevention before this, I was like, oh, these are suicides, right?
sentences.zh: 对我而言，因为我之前有自杀干预的背景，我当时想：哦，这些其实就是自杀，对吧？

sentences.en: In addition to being homicides, suicide, we know how to prevent suicide.
sentences.zh: 除了谋杀之外，这也是自杀，我们懂得如何预防自杀。

sentences.en: There's a ton of wonderful research about suicide prevention and strategies that we can use.
sentences.zh: 有大量关于自杀干预的精彩研究以及我们可以采用的策略。

sentences.en: But we're not using it here because we're not thinking of them like that.
sentences.zh: 但我们在这里没有使用它们，因为我们没有把他们看作是自杀者。

sentences.en: We're thinking of them as these horrific homicides that they are.
sentences.zh: 我们把他们看作是他们所制造的那些可怕的谋杀案的制造者。

sentences.en: But when we think about homicide,
sentences.zh: 但当我们考虑谋杀时，

sentences.en: we think about things like deterrents and armed officers and all these things that won't work if the person is going in planning to die in the act.
sentences.zh: 我们想到的是震慑、武装警卫以及所有这些手段，而如果此人本身就打算在行动中死去，这些手段将毫无用处。

sentences.en: And so it really shifts your thinking.
sentences.zh: 所以这真的会改变你的思维方式。

sentences.en: And simple things like giving schools and organizations more suicide prevention resources and suicide prevention training could be really helpful here.
sentences.zh: 一些简单的事情，比如为学校和机构提供更多自杀干预资源和自杀干预培训，在这里会非常有用。

sentences.en: It seems like one simple answer is to stop the proliferation of guns.
sentences.zh: 一个简单的答案似乎就是遏制枪支泛滥。

sentences.en: I mean, I know everybody says that guns kill people.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我知道每个人都说枪支杀人。

sentences.en: And we – well, I mean, people kill people, guns kill people, people with guns kill people.
sentences.zh: 而我们——我的意思是，人杀人，枪杀人，带着枪的人杀人。

sentences.en: But, I mean, what are the policy changes that could be made in our current environment that would help stem the prevalence of these mass shootings?
sentences.zh: 但是，我的意思是，在我们当前的环境下，可以做出哪些政策改变来帮助遏制这些大规模枪击事件的蔓延？

sentences.en: Yeah, gun policy is something we looked really closely at.
sentences.zh: 是的，枪支政策是我们密切研究过的问题。

sentences.en: We actually built a gun database in addition to the mass shooter database.
sentences.zh: 除了大规模枪击案数据库之外，我们实际上还建立了一个枪支数据库。

sentences.en: So we coded every gun used in every mass shooting.
sentences.zh: 所以我们对每一次大规模枪击案中使用的每一把枪进行了编码。

sentences.en: So it's 400 or 500 guns, and we coded how they were obtained, when they were obtained, legally, illegally, if they were changed or modified,
sentences.zh: 大概有400到500把枪，我们记录了它们的获取方式、获取时间、是合法还是非法获取、是否经过改装或改造，

sentences.en: to really try to add data to our conversations around gun violence prevention.
sentences.zh: 以此来努力为围绕枪支暴力预防的讨论增加数据支持。

sentences.en: So we could say, you know, safe storage would have prevented this many people from dying, or a red flag law would have prevented this many people from dying.
sentences.zh: 这样我们就可以说，安全存放本可以阻止这么多人死亡，或者“红旗法”本可以阻止这么多人死亡。

sentences.en: So what the data shows is when it comes to school shooters,
sentences.zh: 因此数据表明，当谈到校园枪手时，

sentences.en: they are all taking their parents' guns or their grandparents' guns because they can't typically afford – or they can't legally buy them because they're kids of that school and they're not 18.
sentences.zh: 他们拿的都是父母或祖父母的枪，因为他们通常买不起——或者他们无法合法购买，因为他们是那个学校的孩子，还不到18岁。

sentences.en: So safe storage campaigns can be really important there.
sentences.zh: 因此安全存放倡议在那里会非常重要。

sentences.en: These are guns that are in the home, that are unsecured, that young people in crisis have access to.
sentences.zh: 这些枪支存放在家中，没有妥善保管，处于危机中的年轻人可以触及它们。

sentences.en: That's something that's got pretty universal support, actually, from gun owners and non-gun owners alike.
sentences.zh: 事实上，无论是枪支所有者还是非枪支所有者，对此都有相当普遍的支持。

sentences.en: We, our data would support red flag laws or extreme risk protection orders because we know that so many of these perpetrators are in crisis, are leaking their plans, are suicidal.
sentences.zh: 我们的数据支持“红旗法”或极端风险保护令，因为我们知道，许多这样的凶手都正处于危机之中，泄露了他们的计划，并有自杀倾向。

sentences.en: So those are laws that allow for guns to be temporarily removed from somebody's possession if they are in danger to sell for others.
sentences.zh: 因此，这些法律允许在某人对他人或自己构成危险时，暂时没收其拥有的枪支。

sentences.en: There's tricky parts about implementing those laws that I think we're still figuring out, but our data would support them.
sentences.zh: 实施这些法律有些棘手的部分，我想我们仍在摸索中，但我们的数据支持它们。

sentences.en: And then any way we can slow down somebody purchasing a gun when they're in crisis.
sentences.zh: 接着，我们可以采取任何能够减缓处于危机中的人购买枪支速度的措施。

sentences.en: So over the summer, we saw a lot of young men on their 18th birthday going out and buying an AR-15.
sentences.zh: 所以在夏天，我们看到很多年轻人一过18岁生日就出去买AR-15。

sentences.en: So anything where we can raise the minimum age, where we can create waiting periods or permit to purchase, it's about slowing that down so you're not able to go out.
sentences.zh: 所以任何能提高最低年龄限制、设立等待期或购买许可的措施，都是为了放慢这个过程，让你无法在冲动之下行事。

sentences.en: When you're in a state of crisis, immediately purchase a firearm and go commit a shooting.
sentences.zh: 当你处于危机状态时，不会立刻去买一把枪然后去制造枪击案。

sentences.en: What about the way that gun manufacturers are marketing?
sentences.zh: 枪支制造商的营销方式又如何呢？

sentences.en: I mean, it seems to me that there is a lot of push toward hyper-masculine feeling, like you need this big gun because it's going to prove that you're a big man.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在我看来，有很多宣传都在渲染一种极度阳刚的感觉，好像你需要这把大枪来证明你是个男子汉。

sentences.en: I mean, what can be done about that?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，对此能做些什么呢？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's an interesting question that we haven't looked too much into.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个有趣的问题，我们还没有做太多深入研究。

sentences.en: So what we do know is that assault weapons are really overrepresented in mass shootings.
sentences.zh: 我们确实知道的是，突击武器在大规模枪击案中的比例严重过高。

sentences.en: So in kind of everyday homicide, it's about 1% of shootings are involving an assault weapon.
sentences.zh: 所以在日常凶杀案中，大约只有1%的枪击案涉及突击武器。

sentences.en: In mass shootings, it's closer to 25%, and that's been increasing over time.
sentences.zh: 但在大规模枪击案中，这一比例接近25%，而且随着时间的推移一直在增加。

sentences.en: I think we might actually be up to like 28% or 29% now.
sentences.zh: 我想我们现在可能已经上升到28%或29%左右了。

sentences.en: They really are used much more frequently.
sentences.zh: 它们确实被更频繁地使用。

sentences.en: Part of that is because you can kill more people faster, and a lot of these perpetrators, their goal is to kill as many people as possible to make the biggest headlines.
sentences.zh: 部分原因是你可以在更短时间内杀死更多人，而许多凶手的目标就是尽可能多地杀死人，以制造最大的轰动效应。

sentences.en: But the other piece of this is there's this sort of ritual around what a mass shooter does, right, and what they look like and what they dress like,
sentences.zh: 但除此之外，这里还有一种围绕大规模枪击者行为的仪式感，对吧？他们看起来是什么样，穿着什么样，

sentences.en: and they study each other and they mimic each other.
sentences.zh: 他们互相研究，互相模仿。

sentences.en: And so I think this assault weapon, AR-15 in particular, but it's become this symbol, right?
sentences.zh: 所以我认为突击武器，特别是AR-15，已经变成了一个象征，对吧？

sentences.en: It has this symbolic value that's kind of even greater than the damage that it can do.
sentences.zh: 它具有一种甚至大于它本身能造成的破坏的象征价值。

sentences.en: And so I think mass shooters are drawn to it in that way as well.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为大规模枪击犯也正是因此而被它吸引。

sentences.en: I don't know if that's marketing or just that social contagion piece of this, but thinking about how do we stop that, I think in particular laws limiting access to assault weapons,
sentences.zh: 我不知道这算不算营销，还是仅仅是社会传染的一部分，但思考我们该如何阻止这一点，我认为特别需要出台限制获取突击武器的法律，

sentences.en: especially for 18- and 19-year-old young men in crisis, are really critical.
sentences.zh: 尤其是针对处于危机中的18、19岁年轻男性，这绝对至关重要。

sentences.en: Are there any other patterns that I have missed asking you about?
sentences.zh: 还有没有我漏掉没问你的其他规律？

sentences.en: Is there like any kind of a geographic pattern that we see to where mass shootings happen?
sentences.zh: 大规模枪击事件的发生地点是否存在某种地理规律？

sentences.en: They happen everywhere.
sentences.zh: 它们到处都在发生。

sentences.en: They are most common in the South and in the West, although West is primarily from the state of California, has a lot of mass shootings.
sentences.zh: 它们在南部和西部最为常见，尽管西部主要来自加利福尼亚州，该州发生的大规模枪击案很多。

sentences.en: They're a heavily populated state, but they also have a lot of fame-seeking mass shootings, which is interesting.
sentences.zh: 他们是一个人口稠密的州，但同时也发生了很多出于寻求名利心理的大规模枪击案，这很有趣。

sentences.en: School shootings you see occur typically at very large suburban or rural public high schools.
sentences.zh: 校园枪击案通常发生在非常大的郊区或农村公立高中。

sentences.en: I think, you know, we can't say exactly why that is, but theoretically, I think it's about that feeling of not being seen, right?
sentences.zh: 我想，我们无法确切说明原因是什么，但从理论上讲，我认为这与那种没有被看到的感觉有关，对吧？

sentences.en: Like not having people notice you or pay attention to you, it's just a lot easier to not be seen in these really big high schools.
sentences.zh: 就像没有人注意到你或关注你一样，在这些非常大的高中里，不被注意到要容易得多。

sentences.en: These are young men who typically have really no one that they're connecting with.
sentences.zh: 这些年轻男性通常觉得生活中没有跟任何人建立连接。

sentences.en: We do have kind of a communities database that – and so all of this, by the way, you can download for free and analyze and, you know, play with.
sentences.zh: 我们确实有一个社区数据库——顺便说一句，所有这些数据你都可以免费下载、分析并进行研究。

sentences.en: And it's been downloaded thousands of times by researchers and journalists and policymakers.
sentences.zh: 研究人员、记者和政策制定者已经下载了数千次。

sentences.en: So our goal was to really get this out into the public for people to use it.
sentences.zh: 所以我们的目标真的是把这些公之于众，供大家使用。

sentences.en: So there's a whole community database where we track kind of location and community characteristics of things.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们有一个完整的社区数据库，用于追踪各种事物的地理位置和社区特征。

sentences.en: Nothing has really jumped out yet.
sentences.zh: 目前还没有什么特别突出的规律。

sentences.en: You know, it's one of those we can't exactly predict who's going to do this.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是那种我们无法准确预测谁会做出这种事的情况。

sentences.en: We can't exactly predict where it's going to happen, but there's no real exact profile.
sentences.zh: 我们无法准确预测它会发生在哪里，而且也没有什么真正确切的个人画像。

sentences.en: It's kind of – it changes constantly sort of with each shooting that occurs.
sentences.zh: 它基本上是随着每一次枪击案的发生而不断变化的。

sentences.en: Are there any other policy changes that you're advocating for that would really make a difference here?
sentences.zh: 你还在倡导哪些真正能带来改变的其他政策调整吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, so in our book, we came up with over 30 different potential prevention strategies.
sentences.zh: 是的，所以在我们的书中，我们提出了30多种不同的潜在预防策略。

sentences.en: And we tried to organize it around things individuals can do, things institutions can do, and then things as a society that we need to do.
sentences.zh: 我们试图围绕个人能做的事、机构能做的事以及作为一个社会我们需要做的事来组织这些策略。

sentences.en: And I think the society stuff is a heavier lift.
sentences.zh: 我认为社会层面的工作难度更大。

sentences.en: And I think we get stuck there sometimes and we can feel paralyzed when the societal level stuff is not happening.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我们有时会卡在那里，当社会层面的行动迟迟没有进展时，我们会感到瘫痪。

sentences.en: But we do.
sentences.zh: 但我们必须行动。

sentences.en: We need gun control laws.
sentences.zh: 我们需要枪支管制法律。

sentences.en: We need crisis response teams in schools.
sentences.zh: 我们需要学校设立危机应对小组。

sentences.en: But then there's these things at the institutional level.
sentences.zh: 但除此之外，还有这些机构层面的事情。

sentences.en: So things like anonymous reporting systems or crisis response teams or training in crisis intervention and suicide prevention or safe storage campaigns or teaching media literacy and social-emotional learning.
sentences.zh: 比如匿名举报系统、危机应对小组、危机干预和自杀干预培训、安全存放倡议，或者教授媒体素养和社交情感学习。

sentences.en: There's things we really can be doing that the data would say could have a difference.
sentences.zh: 有些事情我们确实可以去做，数据表明这些事情能够带来改变。

sentences.en: And then even at the individual level, you know, some of my favorite stories are people we interviewed who planned to do a mass shooting and changed their mind.
sentences.zh: 而且甚至在个人层面，你知道，我最喜欢的一些故事是，我们采访过一些曾计划进行大规模枪击但最终改变主意的人。

sentences.en: And when they changed their mind, and some of these were even men who were at the school with the gun in their backpack and changed their mind.
sentences.zh: 当他们改变主意时——其中甚至有些人当时就在学校里，背包里还装着枪，但他们还是改变了主意。

sentences.en: And it tends to be a human connection, right?
sentences.zh: 这往往源于人与人之间的连接，对吧？

sentences.en: Somebody connecting with them, somebody getting them through the moment, somebody giving them a little bit of hope, somebody seeing them.
sentences.zh: 有人与他们建立连接，有人陪伴他们度过那一刻，有人给他们带去一丝希望，有人真正看见了他们。

sentences.en: One in particular, this man has a TED Talk, Aaron Stark.
sentences.zh: 其中有一个人特别典型，这个人有个TED演讲，名叫亚伦·斯塔克。

sentences.en: But he talks about how he was planning on doing a mass shooting.
sentences.zh: 他讲述了自己当时是如何计划实施大规模枪击的。

sentences.en: And kind of the day before, he went over to his friend's house and his friend's mom had baked a pie because he was coming over, right?
sentences.zh: 就在事发前一天左右，他去了朋友家，朋友的妈妈因为他要来特意烤了一个派，对吧？

sentences.en: And sitting down and eating that pie was – it stopped him from doing a mass shooting.
sentences.zh: 坐在那里吃那个派——这阻止了他去实施大规模枪击。

sentences.en: Like, it was that powerful of a moment that somebody would have thought, I'm going to make a pie in his honor.
sentences.zh: 当时的情景就是如此震撼，让人不禁觉得：我要为了向他致敬而烤一个派。

sentences.en: It was just a human connection.
sentences.zh: 这其实就是人与人之间的连接。

sentences.en: And so sometimes I think we can get so caught at what we need to do societally that we sometimes forget that we can all just be baking pies for each other.
sentences.zh: 所以有时我觉得，我们在社会层面上需要做的事考虑得太多，以至于有时忘了我们其实都可以为彼此烤烤派。

sentences.en: You never know when that connection is actually having a really meaningful moment for somebody.
sentences.zh: 你永远不知道那种连接什么时候会给某人带来真正意义深远的时刻。

sentences.en: And you have interviewed a number of mass shooters personally, right?
sentences.zh: 而且你亲自采访过不少大规模枪击案的凶手，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, how did you go about that?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你是怎么着手做这件事的？

sentences.en: How did you find them and convince them to talk to you?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么找到他们并说服他们接受你采访的？

sentences.en: Why would they talk to you?
sentences.zh: 他们为什么会愿意跟你谈？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So before I went to graduate school, before I was an academic, I worked with men facing the death penalty as an investigator.
sentences.zh: 所以在去读研究生之前，在我成为学者之前，我曾作为调查员与面临死刑的男性共事过。

sentences.en: And I developed their psychosocial life histories for their sentencing hearings.
sentences.zh: 我为他们的量刑听证会撰写了他们的心理社会生活史。

sentences.en: And so to me, it wasn't that big of a stretch to just say, well, let's just go talk to them, right?
sentences.zh: 所以对我来说，直接说“好吧，我们去和他们谈谈吧”，并不是什么跨度很大的事，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, let's go ask them why they did it.
sentences.zh: 就像是，我们去问问他们为什么要这么做。

sentences.en: And people looked at me like I was out of my mind.
sentences.zh: 人们看着我，就像我疯了一样。

sentences.en: But I just wrote a letter to every living perpetrator I could find who was incarcerated, incarcerated for life.
sentences.zh: 但我只是给所有我能找到的、在世的、被判处终身监禁的凶手都写了一封信。

sentences.en: Most of them die in the act, like we talked about.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所讨论的，他们大多数人在行凶时就死了。

sentences.en: Most of them either kill themselves or are killed.
sentences.zh: 他们大多数要么自杀，要么被击毙。

sentences.en: So we identified, I want to say, 32 maybe who are living.
sentences.zh: 所以我们确认了——我想说是大约 32 个在世的凶手。

sentences.en: I sent just, you know, letters, cold letters saying that I was a researcher and I wanted to talk to them.
sentences.zh: 我只是发了信，你知道，一封冷冰冰的信，说我是一名研究人员，我想和他们谈谈。

sentences.en: I didn't want to talk about their crime.
sentences.zh: 我不想谈论他们的犯罪行为。

sentences.en: I only wanted to talk about the buildup to the crime and what their life was like up to the crime.
sentences.zh: 我只想谈谈犯罪之前的酝酿过程，以及他们在犯罪之前的生活是怎样的。

sentences.en: I said, you weren't going to get paid.
sentences.zh: 我说，你们不会得到报酬。

sentences.en: I would never use your name.
sentences.zh: 我绝不会使用你们的名字。

sentences.en: You weren't going to get any fame or attention out of this.
sentences.zh: 你们也不会从中获得任何名气或关注。

sentences.en: The goal of this project is to prevent mass shootings in the future.
sentences.zh: 这个项目的目标是预防未来发生大规模枪击事件。

sentences.en: And I got, well, I got a number of responses.
sentences.zh: 结果，我收到了不少回复。

sentences.en: I got some attorneys who said they can't because they're in appeals.
sentences.zh: 我收到了一些律师的回信，说他们因为案件在上诉而不能接受采访。

sentences.en: I got two very angry, kind of I hate psychologists, don't contact me.
sentences.zh: 我收到了两封非常愤怒的信，大概意思是“我讨厌心理学家，别联系我”。

sentences.en: But I got seven perpetrators who wrote back and said they wanted to be interviewed.
sentences.zh: 但我收到了七名凶手的回信，他们说希望接受采访。

sentences.en: And from those seven, I was able to talk to five.
sentences.zh: 从这七个人当中，我最终和五个人进行了交谈。

sentences.en: Now, that's not a huge sample.
sentences.zh: 当然，这并不是一个庞大的样本。

sentences.en: It's a small group.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很小的群体。

sentences.en: When you compare it to there's only 30 something living, it's a little better.
sentences.zh: 当你把它与在世的仅三十多人相比时，情况稍微好了一点。

sentences.en: And of course, the ones who talk to me are not necessarily representative of all perpetrators.
sentences.zh: 当然，那些跟我交谈的人并不一定能代表所有的凶手。

sentences.en: These are perpetrators who are invested in kind of telling their story, I guess, who have a lot of shame and regret, I would say,
sentences.zh: 这些凶手是那种热衷于讲述自己故事的人，我想，他们有着极大的羞耻感和悔恨感，可以说，

sentences.en: and are trying to in some way do something positive.
sentences.zh: 并且正试图以某种方式做一些积极的事情。

sentences.en: And so they all, the ones you spoke to expressed regret.
sentences.zh: 所以他们都——你交谈过的那些人都表达了悔意。

sentences.en: They were sorry for what they had done.
sentences.zh: 他们为自己所做的事感到抱歉。

sentences.en: They did.
sentences.zh: 他们的确如此。

sentences.en: Some of them, it had been 20 years.
sentences.zh: 对其中一些人来说，事情已经过去20年了。

sentences.en: You know, some of them, it had been a few years.
sentences.zh: 你知道，对另一些人来说，已经过去几年了。

sentences.en: And so I would say most of them did not really feel connected or recognize the self that did that, right?
sentences.zh: 所以我想说，他们大多数人并不觉得自己与那个做出那种行为的自我有真正的连接或认同，对吧？

sentences.en: They felt kind of disconnected from it.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得自己与那段经历有些脱节。

sentences.en: And so we're able to reflect on it.
sentences.zh: 因此他们能够对此进行反思。

sentences.en: So what are you working on now?
sentences.zh: 那么你现在在研究什么？

sentences.en: Are there other research questions that you're hoping to be able to answer as you continue collecting this data?
sentences.zh: 在你继续收集数据的过程中，还有其他什么研究问题是你希望能够解答的吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, so we're constantly revising and updating the database.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们一直在修正和更新数据库。

sentences.en: And a lot of that is based on kind of users' feedback.
sentences.zh: 这很大程度上是基于用户的反馈。

sentences.en: So we will be putting out version six at the end of this year, which will include all of the mass shootings from 2022 and then also some new variables.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们将在今年年底发布第六版，其中将包括 2022 年的所有大规模枪击事件以及一些新的变量。

sentences.en: So, for example, the role of SSRI drugs got a lot of attention over the summer from some policymakers.
sentences.zh: 例如，今年夏天，SSRIs（选择性5-羟色胺再摄取抑制剂）药物的作用引起了许多政策制定者的广泛关注。

sentences.en: So we went through and we coded who was taking an SSRI so we could kind of add data to that conversation.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们仔细梳理并编码了谁在服用 SSRI，以便我们能为该话题补充相关数据。

sentences.en: We had a number of people ask about height and weight of perpetrators with the impression that they're small.
sentences.zh: 有许多人询问凶手 身高和体重 的情况，因为他们觉得凶手体型较小。

sentences.en: So we're adding that.
sentences.zh: 所以我们把这个也加上了。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So we add things that people come up with.
sentences.zh: 所以我们会把人们想到的东西都添加进去。

sentences.en: We just, our last version, added all of the ACEs, the Adverse Childhood Experiences scores, because people were interested in that.
sentences.zh: 我们刚在上一版中添加了所有的 ACE，即童年逆境经历评分，因为大家对此很感兴趣。

sentences.en: So we're constantly revising the database.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们一直在不断修正数据库。

sentences.en: Let me, can I ask, I want to ask, why just SSRIs and what would they be taking these for?
sentences.zh: 请问，我可以问一下吗，我想问：为什么单单关注 SSRIs？他们服用这些药物是为了治疗什么？

sentences.en: Because, I mean, they could be taking drugs for ADHD.
sentences.zh: 因为，我的意思是，他们也可能在服用治疗多动症（ADHD）的药物。

sentences.en: I mean, there are a lot of drugs that young people could be taking.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，年轻人可能会服用的药物有很多。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: So I get a lot of emails from a lot of people who have a lot of ideas about what causes a mass shooting.
sentences.zh: 所以我收到很多电子邮件，来自许多对“是什么导致了大规模枪击”有着各种各样想法的人。

sentences.en: And the one email I get more than anything else is SSRIs.
sentences.zh: 而我收到最多的邮件内容就是关于 SSRIs 的。

sentences.en: And I think it was Marjorie Taylor Greene who brought it up.
sentences.zh: 我想是玛乔丽·泰勒·格林（Marjorie Taylor Greene）首先提出了这一点。

sentences.en: And it got, it kind of went a little bit viral on social media, this idea that it's specifically SSRIs.
sentences.zh: 这个观点在社交媒体上有点病毒式传播开来，大家都觉得罪魁祸首就是 SSRIs。

sentences.en: I will tell you, it's a very, very small proportion of perpetrators that are taking them.
sentences.zh: 我可以告诉你，服药的凶手只占非常非常小的比例。

sentences.en: It's not that.
sentences.zh: 根本不是那么回事。

sentences.en: But we just wanted to add that data point.
sentences.zh: 但我们只是想把这个数据点补充进去。

sentences.en: I'm not sure exactly where that thinking comes from.
sentences.zh: 我不确定这种想法究竟从何而来。

sentences.en: But I get a lot of people have a lot of ideas about things that we should be coding.
sentences.zh: 但我发现很多人对我们应该对哪些内容进行编码都有各种各样的想法。

sentences.en: The other big project we're working on right now is actually coding threats of school shootings.
sentences.zh: 我们目前正在进行的另一个大项目其实是对学校枪击威胁进行编码。

sentences.en: So threats are through the roof, up like 300%.
sentences.zh: 所以威胁事件呈直线飙升，暴增了大约 300%。

sentences.en: We've been tracking threats since 2018.
sentences.zh: 我们从 2018 年开始一直在追踪威胁事件。

sentences.en: And we finally started coding all of them.
sentences.zh: 我们终于开始对所有这些威胁进行编码了。

sentences.en: So we're coding about 2,000 threats of school shootings and trying to look for patterns in terms of how schools are responding, who's doing it, why they're doing it.
sentences.zh: 所以我们正在对大约 2,000 起学校枪击威胁进行编码，并试图寻找模式：学校是如何应对的、是谁在发出威胁、他们为什么要这么做。

sentences.en: I think we've now got a handle on who commits a school shooting.
sentences.zh: 我想我们现在已经大致搞清楚了是谁在实施学校枪击。

sentences.en: What we don't understand is who are these hundreds of kids a year threatening to do a school shooting.
sentences.zh: 我们所不了解的是，每年这数百名扬言要实施学校枪击的孩子到底是谁。

sentences.en: And maybe they are joking or maybe they, you know, and we don't really have a handle on what's going on there.
sentences.zh: 也许他们是在开玩笑，也许他们——你知道，我们并没有真正弄清楚那里到底发生了什么。

sentences.en: Some kids are serving, you know, 10,
sentences.zh: 有些孩子因为在 TikTok 上发了点东西就要服刑 10 年、

sentences.en: 20 year prison sentences for something they posted on TikTok because we just don't have any good guidance about how we should be intervening here.
sentences.zh: 20 年，仅仅因为我们在如何进行干预方面没有任何好的指导方针。

sentences.en: What's the appropriate intervention?
sentences.zh: 什么是适当的干预措施？

sentences.en: So that's what we're working on right now is trying to help schools figure out what to do here.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是我们目前正在努力的方向，试图帮助学校弄清楚在这种情况下该怎么做。

sentences.en: Because I have principals will call me and say, somebody wrote something on the bathroom stall.
sentences.zh: 因为会有校长打电话给我说：“有人在洗手间隔间里写了些东西。”

sentences.en: Should I shut down the district?
sentences.zh: “我是不是该关闭整个学区？”

sentences.en: You know, and I don't know.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我也不知道。

sentences.en: These schools have no training in how to be making these decisions.
sentences.zh: 这些学校根本没有接受过如何做出这些决定的培训。

sentences.en: So we're trying to add some data to that problem.
sentences.zh: 所以我们正试图为这个问题补充一些数据。

sentences.en: Well, this is amazing information.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这些都是了不起的信息。

sentences.en: I really appreciate you talking to me today and wish you the best of luck in this work, which is so important.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你今天接受我的采访，并祝你在这一极其重要的工作中一切顺利。

sentences.en: Thank you, Dr. Peterson.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，彼得森博士。

sentences.en: Thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。
